body: This change breaks something somewhere else, I'd suggest adding a new method instead to make sure this doesn't break other code, easier than trying to squash issues where ever this is used
it was a case of `l - r` always resulting in a positive integer, oops, fixed
Note that the `ptr` for `_data->name` is guaranteed to be valid, but not with a generic `String`, hence the difference, just to prevent any weirdness with these cases
ah! thank u! i would not have suspected
If you're renaming anyway, it would be a good opportunity to allude to the fact that you're doing a `char32_t` comparison specifically. Maybe call it something like `str32_compare` instead?
this is templated, its `char`, `wchar_t`, `char32_t`, `char16_t`, `int`, whatever. it may use `char32_t` inside, but its for whatever cstr type goes in, i think a generic name fits

it needs to be this verbose, bc if `l._data->cname` is null, then `l._data->name.ptr()` is used (the dynamic string) and they are different types (`const char *` vs `const char32_t *`) so it really is calling 4 different functions technically, its like a dynamic delegator function
